title: Extraction of Nuclei from Archived Post-Mortem Tissues for Single-Nucleus Sequencing
author: Malosree Maitra
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-905/v3
materials: Immediately prior to loading the Hoechst stained nuclei on the Chromium system, check to make sure the nuclei are well segregated (nuclei may clump) and recheck sample concentration using a fluorescent microscope like the Evos FL Auto (Thermofisher)
The authors declare no competing financial interests.

steps.title: Weigh and cut frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Cut 30–50 mg of frozen post‑mortem tissue on dry ice with a scalpel, weigh it, transfer to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube on dry ice using a spatula, clean the scalpel and spatula with 70 % ethanol between samples and use a fresh weigh boat for each sample. Optionally, obtain the same total weight by cryosectioning fresh‑frozen tissue. Observe pathogen precautions and wear PPE.

steps.title: Dounce tissue in lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Place the tissue on ice in a dounce tube, add 3 mL ice‑cold lysis buffer, dounce 10 strokes with the loose pestle followed by 5 strokes with the tight pestle, avoiding bubbles and grinding against the tube bottom.

steps.title: Second lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL centrifuge tube, add 2 mL chilled lysis buffer, incubate on ice for 5 min while gently swirling the tube twice.

steps.title: Quench lysis with wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL chilled wash buffer to the lysed tissue and swirl to mix.

steps.title: Filter tissue suspension
steps.instruction: Place a 30 µm MACS SmartStrainer on a 15 mL tube, pipette the lysed suspension onto the filter, and tap gently if flow is blocked to allow passage of the suspension.

steps.title: Centrifuge filtered suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the filtered suspension in a precooled Allegra‑14X centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Decant supernatant
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant in a single motion into a waste beaker (treat as biohazardous waste with bleach). If the pellet dislodges, remove remaining supernatant with a pipette.

steps.title: First nuclei wash
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL nuclei wash buffer to the nuclei pellet with a 10 mL serological pipette and gently pipet 8–10 times to mix.

steps.title: Repeat filter‑spin‑decant
steps.instruction: Repeat the filter (step 5), centrifuge (step 6) and decant (step 7) steps using the resuspended nuclei.

steps.title: Second nuclei wash
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL nuclei wash buffer to the pellet with a 10 mL serological pipette and gently pipet 8–10 times.

steps.title: Repeat spin‑decant
steps.instruction: Repeat the centrifugation (step 6) and decant (step 7) using the resuspended nuclei.

steps.title: Third nuclei wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL nuclei wash buffer to the pellet with a 1000 µL pipette tip and gently pipet 8–10 times.

steps.title: Add OptiPrep to reach 25 % iodixanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 50 % working OptiPrep™ solution to the nuclei suspension and mix well to obtain 2 mL of 25 % iodixanol (OptiPrep) containing nuclei.

steps.title: Prepare OptiPrep cushion
steps.instruction: In a 5 mL Eppendorf tube, prepare 2 mL of 29 % OptiPrep™ solution (the cushion).

steps.title: Layer nuclei onto cushion
steps.instruction: Gently add the 2 mL nuclei suspension on top of the 29 % OptiPrep cushion by pipetting slowly against the tube wall to avoid mixing.

steps.title: Density‑gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the tube in a precooled Eppendorf centrifuge at 10 000 g for 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove supernatant after gradient
steps.instruction: Carefully pour off the supernatant, leaving the smallest possible volume to avoid disturbing the nuclei pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in ≤500 µL nuclei wash buffer using a 1000 µL pipette tip, pipetting 8–10 times until fully dispersed.

steps.title: Estimate nuclei concentration (Trypan blue)
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of the nuclei suspension with 10 µL Trypan blue, load 10 µL of this mixture onto a Countess hemocytometer slide, count nuclei (average human neuronal nucleus ≈10 µm) and record the concentration.

steps.title: Dilute nuclei to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the nuclei suspension with wash buffer to approximately 500 000 nuclei / mL (≈500 nuclei / µL). Adjust as needed; avoid concentrations that cause aggregation.

steps.title: Add Hoechst stain
steps.instruction: Add Hoechst dye to the nuclei suspension at a 1 : 2000 dilution.

steps.title: Optional Flowmi filtration
steps.instruction: Take ≥200 µL of the stained nuclei, filter through a 40 µm Flowmi pipette tip filter with a 1 mL pipette, then proceed to counting and loading.

steps.title: Load sample onto hemocytometer for imaging
steps.instruction: Place 10 µL of the nuclei suspension on a disposable hemocytometer slide and insert the slide into the Evos microscope.

steps.title: Capture fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Set the Evos to 10X magnification and acquire DAPI and bright‑field images of the entire hemocytometer grid for counting and record‑keeping.

steps.title: Prepare RT Master Mix (Chromium)
steps.instruction: In parallel with steps 22‑24, make the Reverse‑Transcription Master Mix and aliquot the appropriate volumes of master mix and nuclease‑free water into PCR tubes according to the number of nuclei to be captured, following 10× Genomics Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D (or later).

steps.title: Load Chromium chip and generate GEMs
steps.instruction: Load the prepared nuclei suspension onto the Chromium Chip and run the Chromium controller to encapsulate nuclei in droplets (GEMs) according to the Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D.

steps.title: cDNA synthesis and library construction
steps.instruction: Perform reverse transcription, cDNA amplification, and library preparation exactly as described in the Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D; the resulting libraries are compatible with Illumina sequencing.

steps.title: Sequence libraries on Illumina platform
steps.instruction: Sequence the libraries on an Illumina HiSeq 4000 (or equivalent), loading two samples per lane to obtain ~100 000 reads per nucleus using default CellRanger parameters.

steps.title: Generate reference and align reads
steps.instruction: Build a pre‑mRNA reference with `cellranger mkref` (v2.0.1) using the GRCh38‑1.2.0 transcriptome, then run `cellranger mkfastq` (v2.1.0) to demultiplex FASTQ files, and finally run `cellranger count` with default settings to align reads, assign cell barcodes, and count UMIs.

steps.title: Custom filtering of nuclei data
steps.instruction: Load the raw gene‑barcode matrices into R (Seurat v2.2.0/2.3.0) with `Read10X`, create Seurat objects (`CreateSeuratObject`), merge them (`MergeSeurat`), remove mitochondrial genes and genes not detected in any nucleus, then filter out nuclei with ≤110 detected genes and nuclei in the top 0.5 % of UMI counts (potential multiplets). Optionally, fit a three‑component normal mixture to the UMI distribution and retain barcodes with >0.95 probability of belonging to the non‑neuronal or neuronal components and <0.05 probability of belonging to the noise component.
